program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 2000

source_provenance: Sider Scholar + NCBI PubMed exact-source verification
cumulative PMID collision index covering prior enrichment waves and current branch

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 2000

waves.focus: Small randomized trial in 18 female endurance athletes found acute beetroot juice improved selected ventilatory variables and increased VO2max modestly versus placebo; sample size was very small and results are specific to trained women.

Double-blind crossover trial in 18 male basketball players found milk-protein supplementation increased erythrocyte glutathione but did not accelerate recovery of muscle function across a congested three-game schedule; playing time was a stronger recovery determinant.

Systematic review of 16 studies found limited, mixed evidence for acute carbohydrate, beetroot and sodium-citrate use in young athletes, highlighting the thin evidence base and need for age-specific guidance rather than extrapolation from adults.

Double-blind randomized fortification trial in iron-deficient women found some prebiotic-plus-iron flour combinations increased liver-function and renal markers, suggesting that fortification safety outcomes can vary by compound and matrix.

Multicenter double-blind RCT found a defined oral multi-strain probiotic did not reduce vulvovaginal infections during pregnancy and did not colonize the vagina with the administered strains; direct product-specific null evidence.

Randomized double-blind crossover study in eight healthy adults found short-term high-dose cocoa flavanols did not clearly increase Bifidobacterium or Lactobacillus and were not consistent with a prebiotic effect; tiny mechanistic null.

Open-label randomized trial in cirrhosis found probiotic with or without zinc did not reduce hepatic-encephalopathy recurrence, ammonia or MELD score, though quality-of-life and selected sleep outcomes improved; recurrence null is clinically important.

Double-blind RCT in type 2 diabetes with periodontal disease tested synbiotic supplementation alongside nonsurgical periodontal therapy; combination with standard periodontal treatment limits attribution of metabolic and inflammatory changes to the synbiotic alone.

Double-blind RCT in 70 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin found a branded resistant-starch prebiotic improved fasting/postprandial glucose and GLP-1 but not HbA1c, insulin or HOMA-IR over 12 weeks; product-specific adjunctive evidence.

Systematic review found mixed evidence for anti-inflammatory diets, probiotics, fish oil and vitamin D in schizophrenia-related metabolic and symptom outcomes; heterogeneity and adherence barriers preclude broad recommendations.

Double-blind RCT in men with obesity evaluated probiotic supplementation during 30% caloric restriction; any body-composition or psychobiological effects must be interpreted as adjunctive to a strong diet intervention.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 10 RCTs found probiotics did not significantly improve MMSE, MoCA, memory, attention, language or visuospatial outcomes in MCI/Alzheimer's disease; domain effects were heterogeneous and nonsignificant.
Review of Rhodiola polysaccharides focuses on extraction, structure and predominantly preclinical bioactivities; useful chemistry/mechanistic context but not evidence for human efficacy.

Meta-analysis of 15 RCTs reported better cognitive and daily-function outcomes with Ginkgo extract plus donepezil versus donepezil alone in vascular dementia, but combination therapy and source-trial quality constrain inference about Ginkgo alone.

Randomized trial in 120 older patients with ischemic cerebrovascular disease reported better neurologic, inflammatory and hemorheology outcomes with Ginkgo extract added to conventional care; adjunctive design limits monotherapy inference.

Narrative review emphasizes that most positive Ginkgo dementia evidence applies to the standardized EGb 761 extract rather than generic Ginkgo products; clinical heterogeneity and incomplete mechanism remain key boundaries.

Systematic review found only nine eligible Bacopa-related schizophrenia studies and a mixture of mechanistic/preclinical and limited clinical evidence; claims of symptom benefit require much stronger human replication.

Scoping review found inverse associations between vitamin D status and several addictive/impulse-control conditions but substantial methodological limitations and sparse intervention evidence; deficiency association should not be treated as treatment efficacy.

Prospective pregnancy cohort found serum vitamin D levels were not significantly associated with depressive symptoms across pregnancy after adjustment; a change-score signal attenuated with covariate control.

Systematic review identified several non-guideline therapies with urinary-risk or stone-formation signals, including cranberry juice, magnesium compounds, EPA, probiotics and herbs, but intervention diversity and limited replication prevent simple recommendations.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found bariatric surgery altered pharmacokinetics for some drugs and supplements but not consistently for calcium, ferritin or zinc; heterogeneity and missing data made most supplement-PK conclusions uncertain.

USPSTF evidence review found routine iron supplementation reduced maternal iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anemia at term but did not clearly improve major maternal or infant clinical outcomes; screening evidence remained absent.

Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs in prediabetes found vitamin D modestly reduced progression to type 2 diabetes and increased regression to normoglycemia, though the effect size was small and clinical applicability depends on population and regimen.

Systematic review of isotopically measured iron absorption in infants and young children supports current supplementation guidance and identifies ascorbic acid as an absorption enhancer, while lactoferrin/prebiotic strategies remain promising but insufficiently established.

Empirical analysis of 277 adverse-event meta-analyses found inverse publication bias in roughly 14-16% and showed poor-to-moderate agreement of visual assessments, reinforcing that safety evidence synthesis requires direction-aware bias checks and qualitative review.
